claims.statement: Two GitHub Actions workflows divide the operational surface: continuous_integration.yml gates pushes and pull requests to master and develop on ubuntu-26.04, and docker.yml publishes an image on push to develop; neither is a release workflow, so no workflow runs dist.sh, docker.sh, desktop.sh or cargo publish.

Both CI and the Docker publish workflow trigger on a push to develop, but nothing orders them: the image tags come from the git ref via docker/metadata-action and the publish job has no dependency on the build job, so a change can be published as a container image while the CI verdict on that same commit is still running, or after it has failed.

CI sets SKIP_TRUNK=true at job level and builds the web UI exactly once in a dedicated step (cd frontend && trunk build --release) into target/assets; every later cargo invocation reuses those assets, so the wasm payload is compiled once instead of once per clippy, build and test run.

CI installs trunk by extracting a release tarball pinned by TRUNK_VERSION=0.21.14 rather than building it from source, and the Dockerfile downloads the same pinned version as its musl build, keeping the bundled UI reproducible across CI and the published image.

The wasm32-unknown-unknown target exists in CI solely for the trunk build: frontend/ declares its own [workspace], so no cargo invocation in the job compiles the Leptos app, and llvm-tools-preview is present only because cargo-llvm-cov requires it.

CI runs sudo apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=3 update before any install because the runner image bakes its apt lists at image-build time and Ubuntu rolls superseded .debs out of the pool when a newer point version lands, so installing against the cached lists 404s; the retries also cover transient failures of the refresh itself.

CI installs mame-tools, xdelta3 and ffmpeg solely as reference implementations for the format crates' tests — chdman for the chd-rs comparisons, xdelta3 for xdelta-rs, ffmpeg for the LaserDisc AVI fixtures — because those suites skip rather than fail when the reference binary is missing. ctrtool, maxcso and flips are absent, so the cia-rs, xso-rs and xps-rs interop suites skip on every CI run and remain a local responsibility, while oxyromon's own CIA import test runs in-process with no skip guard.

CI enforces the feature matrix with two clippy passes: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features oxyromon/server (package-qualified because --workspace selects several packages) and cargo clippy --no-default-features --features use-rustls,mcp --all-targets, the latter existing because server implies mcp and can never exercise the mcp-without-server build, which is itself a shipped artifact.

Any code reachable from src/mcp must compile with no server cfg active: server-only pieces such as SseMessage, the sse_tx field, with_sse and mcp_http_service are each behind #[cfg(feature = "server")], so referencing them outside that boundary fails the mcp-without-server clippy pass.

The mcp-only feature combination is linted but never executed in CI: clippy --all-targets compiles test targets without running them, so runtime coverage of the stdio server comes from the llvm-cov run under oxyromon/server, where tests/mcp_stdio.rs (gated #![cfg(feature = "mcp")]) compiles and drives the real binary over stdin/stdout.
The CI compile gate fails on hard errors rather than on new lints: neither clippy invocation passes -D warnings, no manifest declares a [lints] section, and the workflow contains no cargo fmt step.

CI runs the whole workspace test suite through cargo llvm-cov --workspace --features oxyromon/server --lcov --output-path lcov.info and uploads that gitignored lcov.info to Codecov with secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN.

CI additionally builds cargo build --release --features server, exercising the release profile (lto thin, codegen-units 1, panic abort) that the artifact users receive and that debug builds never test.

OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY is re-read on every run and never persisted: main.rs uses it as the directory for oxyromon.db, creating the directory and file if absent, then opens the pool, whose establish_connection runs the embedded sqlx::migrate!() migrator — so a failing migration breaks every subcommand at startup.

OXYROMON_ROM_DIRECTORY and OXYROMON_TMP_DIRECTORY are bootstrap-only: they are consulted inside get_rom_directory/get_tmp_directory only when no ROM_DIRECTORY/TMP_DIRECTORY settings row exists, and the chosen value is immediately written to the database, so on any existing database the row wins and changing the environment variable has no effect; moving a library requires oxyromon config.

Stored directory settings are canonicalized on read via get_canonicalized_path, so a configured directory that has been deleted or unmounted yields None and re-triggers the environment/default bootstrap rather than erroring.

OXYROMON_LOG_LEVEL is consumed by env_logger's Builder::from_env inside the subcommand guard, its filter pushed into log::set_max_level and its logger wrapped in indicatif_log_bridge's LogWrapper over the process-wide MultiProgress; because this init sits inside if let Some((subcommand, ...)), a run with no subcommand loads no .env, installs no logger, opens no database, and exits successfully.
dotenvy's dotenv().ok() runs at the top of the subcommand branch, so a .env in the working directory supplies OXYROMON_* values before any of them is read; .env is gitignored.

No CI step, Dockerfile or cross build sets DATABASE_URL or SQLX_OFFLINE; the sqlx query macros are verified at compile time against the committed .sqlx/ snapshots, so a query or migration change left unprepared by cargo sqlx prepare -- --features server breaks CI, the container build and the release matrix, not only the author's machine.

CI compiles only the rustls backend: use-native-tls, bare --no-default-features and every macOS/Windows target are never built there, so an OpenSSL-only break is invisible until someone or a packager builds it, and nothing enforces that exactly one TLS backend is selected.

docker.yml builds and pushes ./Dockerfile with tags from docker/metadata-action, so automated pushes never produce the version-pinned tag; it exists only when docker.sh, which pushes <version> and latest, is run by hand.

The single Alpine-based container image fixes the runtime paths by environment (OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY=/data, OXYROMON_ROM_DIRECTORY=/roms with matching VOLUMEs) so a container ignores host platform directories, deliberately does not set SKIP_TRUNK so the wasm UI is built inside the image with trunk's musl build (no gcompat), and ends in CMD ["oxyromon"] with no subcommand, which makes a bare docker run a successful no-op.

With the mcp subcommand or the server's /mcp mount, stdout carries MCP JSON-RPC, so code reachable from the MCP server must not print to stdout and should use log macros or the progress helpers instead.

CI pins no Rust toolchain: no rust-toolchain.toml exists, so dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable installs whatever stable is current when the workflow runs, while the only declared MSRV anchor is rust-version = "1.94.0" in Cargo.toml's [workspace.package], repeated in AGENTS.md, and nothing in CI enforces it; cargo-llvm-cov is likewise installed unpinned, so a new stable release can break the gate with no repository change.

CI never compiles the configuration with neither mcp nor server, which is exactly the arm where src/database.rs selects max_connections = 1 and PRAGMA locking_mode = EXCLUSIVE instead of 5 connections with NORMAL: the first clippy pass always enables server and the second always enables mcp, so a cfg_if mistake on the single-connection branch surfaces only for packagers and bare cargo builds.

The env-var surface is what makes the MCP stdio test hermetic: tests/mcp_stdio.rs spawns the built binary with OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY pointed at a TempDir and OXYROMON_LOG_LEVEL=off, so migrations and catalog writes land in a throwaway database and log output cannot corrupt the JSON-RPC framing read from stdout.

The apt packages are build-and-test-only: the shipped oxyromon binary shells out to none of them, since get_version() in src/chd.rs, src/cia.rs, src/xdelta.rs, src/xps.rs, src/xso.rs, src/archive.rs, src/nsz.rs and src/rvz.rs returns "built-in" and the work runs through the workspace crates; no module invokes an external tool.

Reference-tool discovery is an extension point for running the interop suites off-distro: the chd-rs and xso-rs harnesses read $CHDMAN, $FFMPEG and $MAXCSO as an absolute path first and otherwise scan $PATH for the binary, skipping the test with a message when neither yields a file, whereas the xdelta3 and flips suites probe only the bare command name on PATH and offer no override variable.

The repository's CI surface contains exactly two workflow files; AGENTS.md's OpenWiki block refers to a scheduled OpenWiki GitHub Actions workflow that refreshes openwiki/, but no such file exists in .github/workflows, so the wiki refresh cadence is not defined or gated by anything in the current tree.
The container build installs GNU tar but not cmake: GNU tar is needed only on Alpine for the web UI's fetch-webawesome.sh hook, and cmake left the package list once chd-rs stopped using libflac-sys.
